long_biography.plain_text:
Iraq’s Constitution establishes a federal parliamentary republic in which the Council of Ministers exercises the executive responsibilities assigned to the national government. Led by the prime minister, the council develops public policy, implements laws and coordinates ministries and other federal authorities.

The government’s work extends across national administration, regulation and public services within Iraq’s constitutional system. Presidents, prime ministers and ministers hold time-limited offices, while the government remains the continuing institutional body through which executive functions are performed. The name represents that public institution collectively, rather than any current or former officeholder.
